summary: Three slices. (1) Durable jobs (migration v13: jobs + job_attempts with unique idempotency keys, leased compare-and-set claims, exponential backoff, retry budgets, dead letters, requeue) and crash-safe email dispatch: the job lease, outbox 'sending' and a per-item Message-ID are committed before the provider is called; expired leases are reconciled through MailProvider.find_sent (found / absent / unknown), never resent blind, and unknown becomes 'needs_check' for the operator. (2) Encrypted credential vault: AES-256-GCM per credential (name as AAD) in data/vault.json, key only in the OS keychain via keyring; credential references with fingerprint, rotation, expiry and revocation; crash-recoverable key rotation; secret redaction in the log-record factory; reversible migration from .env; CLI, API and Settings card. (3) Tenancy (migration v14): workspaces, users, memberships (rep/manager/admin), hashed bearer tokens, audit events, and workspace_id on companies, prospects, campaigns, outbox and conversations. Local mode (the default) is unchanged and separately tested. Shared mode (FRANCO_MODE=shared) authenticates tokens and applies a server-side route allowlist with role permissions and workspace ownership checks (another workspace's record answers 404); every unlisted API route is refused; credential management needs admin of the installation workspace; denials and allowed mutations are audited. Owner decisions 2026-10-20: build tenancy anyway; encrypted file plus keychain key; durable sends first. Implementation commits a6deb8c, 4f92ff7 and 3d1aac0. All three acceptance criteria have passing tests. Reviewed by the owner on 2026-10-20. Verification remains mocked: no Gmail/SMTP sandbox or real OS keychain was exercised, so this is not live-readiness evidence.

tests.log: harness/parity/evidence/logs/P01-full-suite.log (703 passed, 20 skipped: environment-gated Codex CLI and packaging tests)

P01-A1.evidence: tests/test_p01_tenancy.py, end to end through the dashboard HTTP layer in shared mode with three workspaces. Cross-tenant IDs: a rep in 'acme' calling approve/reject/edit/resolve on a 'globex' outbox item, or reading a 'globex' company's contacts, gets 404; the item stays pending_review; 5 'denied' audit events are written to acme naming the target, none into globex. Lists (outbox, contact search, companies) return only the caller's workspace, and bulk approval needs a manager and stays inside the workspace. Credentials: a rep, a manager and another workspace's admin each get 403 on POST /api/settings/env, POST /api/settings/test-instantly (zero external requests), GET /api/settings, GET /api/secrets and POST /api/secrets/{name}/revoke; .env is not written; each denial is audited. The installation admin succeeds. Also covered: missing, wrong and revoked tokens and disabled users get 401; tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes; every API route not on the allowlist answers 403 in shared mode, even for the installation admin; every allowlisted route exists; the audit log is manager+ and workspace-scoped; local mode needs no token, keeps every route and the localhost guard.

P01-A2.evidence: tests/test_p01_durable_sends.py with tests/durable_send_worker.py: a real subprocess sends through a file-backed fake provider and SIGKILLs itself (returncode -9) after the provider's durable acknowledgement and before Franco records the send. A second process reconciles: the mailbox still holds exactly 1 message, the outbox row is 'sent' with the same Message-ID, and the job attempt outcome is lease_expired_found. Also covered: kill before acknowledgement (sent exactly once on replay, same Message-ID; a further cycle sends nothing), and kill with an unconfirmable provider (held as needs_check, job dead with code 'unconfirmed', never resent across two recovery cycles). Mocked verification only: Gmail keeping a client-set Message-ID, and Gmail search freshness, have not been exercised against a real or sandbox mailbox.

P01-A3.evidence: tests/test_p01_vault.py. Expired: a credential past expires_at raises CredentialExpired; storing a new value recovers it. Revocation: the ciphertext and nonce are deleted from the file (not hidden); get raises CredentialRevoked; load_env reports {'SERPER_API_KEY': 'revoked'} and discovery.serper becomes unavailable with reason 'SERPER_API_KEY is revoked in the vault'; putting a new value recovers. Recovery also covers a key rotation crashed between file rewrite and keychain update (backup restored, values readable). Redaction: after load_env registers vault secrets, formatted args, f-strings and exception tracebacks in log records all show ***REDACTED***; the Gmail refresh token is redacted; /api/secrets, /api/settings, /api/setup-status and /api/capabilities never contain secret values. Plus: no plaintext in the vault file, mode 0600, ciphertexts bound to names, tampering detected, a missing keychain key locks the vault and refuses to orphan stored secrets, the keyring adapter maps backend errors to VaultLocked, and migrate/unmigrate round-trips .env and the token byte for byte. Keychain tests use an in-memory key or a fake keyring backend; the real OS keychain was not exercised by tests.

limitations: Gmail find_sent searches rfc822msgid first, then recipient + subject + time. Whether Gmail keeps a client-set Message-ID is unverified without a sandbox; the fallback can report FOUND for a different email with the same subject to the same person, which skips a send (no duplicate, but a missed email).
The SMTP adapter only answers FOUND or UNKNOWN (IMAP Sent-folder search), so any SMTP crash mid-send ends in needs_check for the operator.
The legacy Instantly path (campaign deploy and lead upload) is not on the durable job store.
Confirming a needs_check item as sent from the dashboard does not re-time later sequence steps; they keep their staged schedule.

New runtime dependencies cryptography 47.0.0 and keyring 25.7.0 (plus cffi, pycparser, jaraco-*, more-itertools) were added to pyproject, requirements.in and the hashed lock. The lock was regenerated with pip-compile on macOS / Python 3.12 (the documented command uses Python 3.11 via uvx, which is not installed), so keyring's Linux and Windows-only dependencies (SecretStorage/jeepney, pywin32-ctypes) are not in the lock.

The vault is opt-in: until 'franco secrets migrate' runs, secrets stay in plaintext .env as before. The real macOS Keychain path (KeychainKey against the system keyring) was not exercised by automated tests; macOS may prompt once per process to allow access.

A test run during development briefly wrote a fake Gmail token to the checkout's data/gmail_token.json (no real token existed there: the file's birth time was the test run). It was deleted, and the vault tests now redirect TOKEN_FILE to a temp path.

Shared mode exposes only the allowlisted routes: outbox review, contact search, companies, capabilities, me, audit, settings and secrets. Everything else (discovery, import, campaigns, conversations, signals, start/stop, exports and more) is refused in shared mode until it is made tenant-safe.

Workers (sender, writer, handler, prospecting) are not workspace-aware: everything they create lands in the 'local' workspace, and all workspaces send through the installation's single mail identity. Other workspaces only hold data that was assigned to them directly.
Provider credentials are installation-wide, not per workspace; vault entries carry workspace_id='local'.
Shared mode re-runs init_db on every API request (a schema check), and the browser keeps the token in sessionStorage; there is no login page, sessions, password reset or SSO.
Exposing the dashboard beyond localhost stays excluded (dashboard.public): shared mode still relies on the host/origin guard and has no TLS of its own.

Running the CLI during development ('franco users list') migrated the checkout's real data/franco.db from schema v12 to v14. The migrations are additive and the app applies them on its next start anyway; the database held 0 prospects and 0 outbox rows.
Human review was by the owner (Jgomez25), stated in chat; no second reviewer.
